summary: Clallam County: a 1942 lookout also used by the Aircraft Warning Service; the tower is gone, and access to the summit area needs permission.

facts.design: Cowan-type two-story 10x10 cabin on the 1942 state list; the AWS built a 14 x 32 sleeping cabin nearby
facts.status_note: Tower gone. Willhite's access notes concern the Pysht Tree Farm, and entry needs permission.

staffing.as_of: 1942 (Aircraft Warning Service activation; no later staffing found)

access.note: Willhite says permission is needed, though the road is paved to the gate at the community of Pysht.

visit.trail_note: Willhite gives about 4 miles one way on foot or by bike, without saying where it starts. No tower stands to climb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com date the tower to 1942. Willhite places a Cowan-type lookout on a 1942 state list and says the Aircraft Warning Service used an existing state structure. The 1942 date is kept and both accounts are described.

notes_for_editor: Elevation disagrees: the register and FireLookout.com give 900 ft (274 m), and Willhite gives 730 ft. The brief's 274.3 m follows the register; the story does not give an elevation. No source dates the tower's removal, so no removal event is recorded. Staffing is limited to the 1942 Aircraft Warning Service activation. Access notes come from undated trip notes on WillhiteWeb; check current Pysht Tree Farm rules before a visit. Willhite's remark that a hunting permit may be needed is his guess and is left out. No photos added. Used 1 WebSearch and 4 page reads. Fact-check 2026-10-09: Willhite's 4-mile figure has no stated start point, so the story names none.
